notes: Working accepted name Cissus trifoliata (L.) L.; NPSOT lists Cissus incisa and Sicyos trifoliatus as previous names.

target_zone_range_leads.guardrail: No final range decision in Scout.
leads: NPSOT maps the species across Edwards Plateau and Texas Blackland Prairies and links a BONAP county map; exact target-zone county evidence remains for Deep Review.
Central Texas/Hill Country field context is supported by regional horticultural/native-plant sources; do not infer counties from ecoregions.

morphology_candidate.look_here_first: Look first at the thick, slightly succulent 3-parted/trifoliolate leaf and fleshy reddish stem; crush-leaf odor is a supporting field clue, then confirm tendrils and dark berry clusters.
diagnostic_traits: alternate thick or slightly succulent leaves, deeply 3-lobed to trifoliolate
fleshy red to red-brown stems and swollen/warty nodes
berries purple-black to black at maturity

confusers.separator: Cissus trifoliata usually presents thick 3-parted/trifoliolate foliage rather than the palmately 5–7-foliolate Parthenocissus pattern.
Use the thick 3-parted foliage, fetid crushed-leaf odor, stem texture and reproductive structures rather than grape-like berries alone.
